I asked about war production and it has to do with Zrak, and then the second question has to do with the consumption of energy that we are allowing into Sarajevo. And that energy is used for manufacturing ammunition, and we're still letting them have this energy, although we know that they're manufacturing ammunition.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You are not giving evidence. So your position is that the witness is in the position to answer the question or to know such a situation. Why don't you put -- pose such question to the witness yourself?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think I have done so, Excellency. Does he know that anything else was manufactured for war in addition to optical sights, and he said shells and that that required a great deal of energy, electricity, gas, so on. Now I'm going to ask how much was manufactured during the first year. And this is a Muslim document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Dr. Karadzic, I must confess that Ms. -- the submission by Ms. West carries some force in that she is awkwardly placed. She cannot say anything at all about the document and is very, you know, awkwardly placed to comment one way or the other, and I think there is substance in that objection. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We -- the Chamber sustains Ms. West's objection. Move on to another document or another subject.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Excellency. Then I'm going to deal with this some other time. The witness certainly answered that he was aware of this production.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please clarify one thing for us. In that document that refers to Lalic and another person from state security, there is a reference to the brigade commander and the barracks commander. Is this one and the same thing?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO VUJASIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It has to do with me. In that document in one way or the other, it has to do with me; that is to say, a single individual.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. These misunderstandings of military commands with civilian authorities, was that unique to Rajlovac? Are you aware of similar cases?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO VUJASIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was a specific case only with regard to Rajlovac whereas elsewhere there weren't such problems because this has to do with Rajlovac specifically.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you hear, for example, that from Ilidza also a man, Despotovic --

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO VUJASIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pero? Pero Despotovic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I withdraw it. Okay. I withdraw that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, from Rajlovac did you go to a higher or lower position?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO VUJASIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went to a higher position.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. As regards the question regarding Ahatovici, you did not complete your answer. You said the situation around Ahatovici was such.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO VUJASIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 15th, 16th, 17th of May. From Pofalici most people had remained in the area, in the area of Rajlovac, that is. So this led to panic, dissatisfaction. Quite a few of them were put up at the Rajlovac barracks, women, children, and these men. Now, when refugees came or civilians from Ahatovici, there was a culmination of this hatred. That's why it was necessary to make sure that the situation was resolved as soon as possible. That is that set of circumstances that I refer to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On page 18, it was suggested to you -- actually, it was a two-pronged question, that these civilians were detained in different places in Rajlovac and that they were maltreated, and you said that you knew that and that you prevented that. When you said that you knew that, did that have to do with them being detained in Rajlovac?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO VUJASIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were concentrated near the barracks in Rajlovac, but the original part of the facility --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could all other microphones please be switched off. We cannot hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us clarify the matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't think the whole answer of the witness was translated. Could you repeat your answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you repeat your answer.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO VUJASIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The original part of the facility for the civilians that were there, that is to say a special part of the facilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You mentioned Pofalici. Who came to the barracks and why?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO VUJASIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: People who were refugees, women, children, and also men from Pofalici who had fled because they were expelled through Zuc and they had nowhere to go, and then they found shelter in the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What was the ethnicity of these persons from Pofalici?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO VUJASIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Serb ethnicity. I think there were a few Croats there as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What was the ethnicity of these people from Ahatovici?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO VUJASIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Muslim ethnicity and religion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Civilians from Ahatovici, were they your prisoners?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO VUJASIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. Because we were making an effort to free them as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What was the attitude of the officials of Republika Srpska who happened to be in Rajlovac at that point in time? What was their attitude towards these Muslim civilians?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO VUJASIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would say that if it weren't for these people and for the professional soldiers, it would have been a mess. These people who were expelled from Pofalici and then these people came and this was total hatred and the people in Pofalici had their houses burned and people killed, and then there were these people from Ahatovici and that would have been a mess. The position was to have this resolved as soon as possible, to have them released so that they could go and that they be given safe passage.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In the document that refers to crime in Rajlovac, I mean in that document, on page 1 it says there is not enough strength to deal with real criminals. Did you have enough military police to resolve that, and after going to the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, were you in a position to initiate changes in the military police or at least to provide information to that effect that there weren't sufficient forces?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before you answer, Mr. Vujasin, yes, Ms. West.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't know which document that he's talking about, but whichever document it is, this subject matter was not addressed in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President, if I could respond to that. She raised the whole issue of his conflicts with the security agency and with other people, and this can explain a reason for that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 24346 is the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So even in that document --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Actually, can we have that document, 24346.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let us take a look at the third paragraph. It says: There are arrests, searches, and for real criminals there is no strength and will to control or even arrest the real criminals. This is the reason why there was an initiative to disband the military police in Rajlovac, and the corps commander General Galic was made aware of that fact. What can you say about this, the third paragraph, the second part of the third paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO VUJASIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: There weren't enough forces to have proper order in the civilian police and the military police both in Rajlovac. People came who had not been cleared properly. I know there was only one professional policeman, civilian policeman. He was Bozic's relative or son-in-law or something like that. And people who joined the police had not been checked properly. Their quality was not checked properly, and I know that soldiers deserted. They took weapons and -- how do I put this? Later on you see them elsewhere in the police. So it -- the situation was not clear. Now, there wasn't enough strength and then there was this chaos, general chaos.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Who informed the corps commander about this and do you know whether something was done about it?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO VUJASIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The corps commander was made aware of this, and he knew the situation from me personally and from others, and also he toured the area. He sent his units. Sometimes he came on his own, and sometimes he sent others, and he personally had some problems in Ilidza, for instance. In Blazuj, from the commander of the brigade -- or, rather, the Igman Brigade. I personally know that. He was fired at too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was any kind of intervention carried out? Was there any kind of cleansing in the military police? Did anyone do something about this?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO VUJASIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Something was done about this every day in terms of cleansing the police or getting people who were of sound character, or if not then they should be deployed to other units too, and then it was very hard to do that because of the resistance of these people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In this stage which ethnic community was the victim of these criminals?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO VUJASIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say here that it was people behind the lines that were victims. So it was specifically the Serb side. Everybody that happened to be there in Rajlovac, they were robbed and persons misappropriated property to their own benefit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You mentioned the cleansing of Sokolje and Brijesce that you opposed. What do you mean by this cleansing?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO VUJASIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally mean -- well, this is a term that came into being during the war in 1992 in our area; that is to say that the territory should be free for freedom of movement in one's own territory. That's what it means. Now, nothing should be out of control. So cleansing means that this police should be cleansed and done up properly, both.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And who's supposed to be cleansed from the area that's supposed to be cleansed?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO VUJASIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Criminals and those who put up resistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What about civilians?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO VUJASIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are not the subject. They are not the subject. However, I must say that to a large degree they are the victims of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Colonel, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellencies, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You are not tendering 24346 either. Very well. Then that concludes your evidence, Mr. Vujasin. On behalf of the Chamber, I would like to thank you for your coming to The Hague to give it. Now you are free to go, but probably we will rise all together.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I wanted to raise one housekeeping matter before we adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Mr. Vujasin, you may be excused. Please make a safe journey home back -- back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. May I can take this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. This is a follow-up to a discussion that Mr. Robinson and I had yesterday, and it concerns two witnesses currently scheduled for portions of the later -- the last two days of January. I related to Mr. Robinson that the OTP would have significant difficulties with the appearance of the witnesses on those particular days because of a particular personnel issue. He understood and agreed to reschedule the witnesses but expressed concern about his ability to ensure that any resulting gap was absolutely filled. He certainly intends to do so but couldn't be completely confident that the full time that had originally been scheduled for those witnesses would be filled by other witnesses in the aftermath of the rescheduling. And of course that would not be fair to him and to his team in their effort to very fairly and collegially resolve this problem. So I propose to bring it to the attention of the Court, to let you know explicitly how we intended to resolve this problem so that there would be no recrimination if, in fact, he wasn't successful in fully filling the portions of those two days that had -- when the witnesses were originally schedule. And I hope that's satisfactory with the Court. We appreciate very much the Defence's accommodation in this regard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber also appreciates the co-ordination of the parties, and I encourage them to resolve it in a very positive way.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. And one last thing, in a courtroom where a remarkable level of civility and collegiality prevails, I think I'd be remiss if I didn't take this opportunity on behalf of the Prosecution to express our best wishes for the holiday season to everyone involved in these proceedings, including the Judge behind the pole. But we certainly express in our heartfelt way our best wishes to everyone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tieger. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence would also like to join these greetings for all the coming holidays, and also I should like to express my thanks for taking into account the need that I expressed for the timing of our recess in terms of Orthodox holidays.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. I would also like to take this opportunity to express the Chamber's gratitude, sincere gratitude, for the Registry staff, interpreters, court reporters, and the security staff who made it possible for the Chamber to conduct the proceedings in a smooth way. On behalf of the Chamber, I extend to all greetings for a happy holiday season. And amicus curiae.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Whatever our designation may be, on behalf of the stand- by team, Your Honours, I wouldn't want to be thought the Scrooge at this feast and not join in the general well-wishes to all. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Harvey. The hearing is now adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
